Inc., San Diego, California (N6247321D1206); Heffler Contracting Group,* El Cajon, California (N6247321D1207); Korte Construction Co., doing business as The Korte Co., St. Louis, Missouri (N6247321D1208); M. A. Mortenson Co., doing business as M.A. Mortenson Construction, Minneapolis, Minnesota (N6247321D1209); R. A. Burch Construction Co. Inc.,* Ramona, California (N6247321D1210); RQ Construction LLC, Carlsbad, California (N6247321D1211); Sundt Construction Inc., Tempe, Arizona (N6247321D1212); Walsh Federal LLC, Chicago, Illinois (N6247321D1213); Webcor Construction LP, doing business as Webcor Builders, Alameda, California (N6247321D1214); and The Whiting-Turner Contracting Co., Baltimore, Maryland (N6247321D1215), were awarded a combined $99,000,000 to increase the maximum value of a firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, multiple award construction contract for new construction, renovation, and repair of commercial and institutional facilities at various locations in the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Southwest area of operations. The work to be performed provides for, but is not limited to, airport, office, administrative, and religious buildings, communication, vehicle maintenance, barracks, prison, dining, hospital/medical, warehouse, school, and/or retail facilities, armories, parking garages, fire stations, and hotels. The contract consists of a base period of two years and one three-year option period (and a bridge extension of one year), with a combined maximum dollar value not to exceed $3,043,000,000. No funds were obligated at time of award. Future task orders will be primarily funded by Military Construction Navy, operations and maintenance (Navy), or operations and maintenance (Marine Corps) funds. Work will be performed in California (87%), Arizona (5%), Nevada (3%), Utah (2%), Colorado (2%), and New Mexico (1%), and is expected to be completed by November 2026. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with 28 offers received. NAVFAC Southwest, San Diego, California, is the contracting activity.

announcements.text: Pacific Shipyards International,* Honolulu, Hawaii, is awarded a $14,428,074 firm-fixed-price contract (N3220527C1204) for a 75-calendar day shipyard availability for the regular overhaul and dry dock availability of Military Sealift Command’s rescue and salvage vessel USNS Grasp (T-ARS 51). This contract includes a base work package and three unexercised options for additional work and time, which if exercised, would increase the cumulative value of this contract to $14,948,825. Work will be performed in Honolulu, Hawaii, beginning Jan. 11, 2027, and is expected to be completed by March 26, 2027. Fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $14,428,074 are obligated and will expire at the end of the fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured with proposals solicited via the Government wide Point of Entry website and two offers were received. Military Sealift Command, Norfolk, Virginia, is the contracting activity.

announcements.text: Lockheed Martin Corp., Manassas, Virginia, has been awarded a maximum $80,000,000 time-and-materials task order under the General Services Administration Alliant 2 governmentwide acquisition contract for Strategic Mission Planning and Execution System Global Strike Product Support (SMPES GSPS). This task order provides agile software engineering, modernization, continuous maintenance, sustainment, and architectural updates for the operational SMPES GSPS applications suite. Work will be performed at Offutt Air Force Base, Nebraska, and is expected to be completed by Jan. 19, 2030. This task order was a competitive acquisition, and one offer was received. Fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $868,270; and fiscal 2027 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $500,000, are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center, Offutt AFB, Nebraska, is the contracting activity (FA2217-27-F-B001).

announcements.text: The Boeing Co., Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, has been awarded a $16,910,812 modification (P00009) to previously awarded contract FA2363-25-C-B002 for Japan E-767 Airborne Warning and Control System post-delivery support services. This modification provides for the exercise of an option period for the continuation of technical sustainment, engineering, on-site field service representatives, and software maintenance services. The modification does not change the total cumulative face value of the contract of $35,530,249. Work will be performed in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma; San Antonio, Texas; and Hamamatsu Air Base, Japan, and is expected to be completed by Nov. 14, 2027. This contract involves Foreign Military Sales (FMS) to Japan. FMS funds in the amount of $16,910,812 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Hanscom Air Force Base, Massachusetts, is the contracting activity. (Awarded on Nov. 2, 2026).
